title: Topology-preserving NIC-400 migration engine
summary: Evolved migration scripts into a Python engine that reconstructs interconnect topology and preserves source design relationships.

dates.note: First inspected milestone: 2023-05-04. See facts for earlier/later feature stages; this is neither proof of first-ever work nor a formal role/leadership start or shipped release date.

facts.text: Developed an integrated NIC-400 XML/CCXML-to-NCI conversion engine reconstructing source microarchitecture, preserving topology and placement, and applying logged DRC-driven repairs.
Mapped source bus matrices, clock-domain crossings and width conversions into target blocks, rejecting unresolved topology assumptions rather than inventing connectivity.

Added corpus collection, audit tooling, valid/invalid fixtures and source-fidelity assertions; a historical commit reports 4,130 of 4,130 valid configurations DRC-clean and 5 of 5 curated invalid configurations rejected.
Modeled legacy source microarchitecture as nodes, edges and paths, mapping bus matrices, clock crossings and width conversion into target routers and helper blocks.
Built bounded DRC closure with at most six iterations, per-fix fidelity-impact records, initial/iteration/final results and a stop when no further repair progress is possible.
DRC-clean migration is not proof of RTL or functional equivalence: target repairs may introduce helpers or adjust mappings, endpoints and memory maps.

notes: Scripts began in 2023 and expanded in 2024; the integrated engine was introduced in 2026.
The corpus result is a historical commit report; raw execution logs were not independently recovered and tests were not rerun here.
Primary implementation responsibility is documented alongside subsequent fixes by colleagues.

2026-10-27 local Git/source research supplements prior evidence. Authorship supports attributable implementation; shared components and later colleague changes retain separate ownership. No employer tests were rerun.
